author: Mark
title: ICE Gets Shock Gloves and the 'Abolish ICE' Crowd Is About to Need a Fainting Couch
text:
The Department of Homeland Security just allocated $20 million for the purchase of electrified compliance gloves for Immigration and Customs Enforcement agents. The device is called the CTG-5 G.L.O.V.E. — that's Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter — and it's manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC out of Lexington, Kentucky.
The G.L.O.V.E. is a standard patrol glove with a switch-activated electrical mode that delivers a pain stimulus on contact. Think of it as a less-lethal compliance tool that doesn't require an agent to draw a separate weapon or create distance during a physical encounter. John Peters, president of the Institute for the Prevention of In-Custody Deaths, described the sensation in straightforward terms: "It's immediate and sharp, and it will distract you. I call it like a bee sting."
Peters added context on the tactical application: "If the officer is getting any type of resistance from the person, this is certainly an effective tool." The device is designed for situations where suspects are physically non-compliant during apprehension — the exact scenarios that currently escalate into injuries on both sides.
And that's the part the inevitable outrage cycle will conveniently skip over. One official who has used the G.L.O.V.E. in the field offered this: "Since I have started using the G.L.O.V.E., I have not sent any officers to the hospital." Fewer officer injuries. Fewer suspect injuries. A pain stimulus that lasts a moment and leaves no lasting damage. The DHS notice requires agents to complete recertification on the device every two years.
The "abolish ICE" contingent will frame this as militarization of immigration enforcement. Which is a fascinating argument to make about a glove that stings like a bee and reduces hospitalizations. The same people who spent four years demanding police use less-lethal alternatives are now going to lose their minds over a less-lethal alternative.
This is what ICE enforcement looks like when you actually fund it and let the agency do its job. The Biden years hollowed out staffing, tanked morale, and turned immigration agents into airport greeters. The current DHS is rebuilding operational capacity, and the G.L.O.V.E. procurement is one piece of a broader equipment modernization push. Agents who are physically engaging non-compliant subjects during removal operations need tools that de-escalate force, not amplify it.
Somehow, this will be the most controversial glove since O.J.'s.
